newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to up museum security after failed robbery.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to up museum security after failed robbery.

text.p: Egypt will spend 25 million pounds ($7.35 million) on security at the Egyptian Museum after a man tried to steal some Pharaonic treasures, Cairo newspapers reported on Friday.

They said Minister of Culture Farouk Hosni decreed that a state-of-the-art electronic security system be fitted as soon as possible in the museum and particularly in rooms containing valuable gold items.
Police dogs will also patrol the building daily after closing, they added.
Security men currently check the museum twice a day -- before opening and after closing -- while iron bars with gaps between them protect the jewellery rooms.

On Tuesday, an unemployed man hid under a museum showcase until closing time and then broke open several display cases, taking 24 objects including golden bracelets and a gem-encrusted dagger of King Tutankhamun.
He was arrested the next day while trying to escape.
The dailies said this was the third time someone had tried to steal objects from the museum by hiding in it.
